source: វិទ្យាការទប់ស្កាត់ និងកម្ចាត់សមាសភាពបទព្រុងលើដំណាំទុរេន (Prevention and Control of Harmful Organisms on Durian), Cambodian technical extension document compiled with reference to CABI Crop Protection Compendium and durian pest/disease literature, 28pp
text: Anthracnose / leaf spot, caused by the fungus Colletotrichum gloeosporioides, produces brown to dark, often somewhat circular spots on durian leaves, which can enlarge and merge in humid conditions, and can also affect fruit, causing dark sunken lesions on the husk that may extend damage into the flesh in severe cases. The disease is worse in wet, humid weather and spreads readily where infected leaf litter is left to accumulate under the canopy. General control approach: remove and destroy fallen infected leaves and fruit rather than leaving them to compost under the tree, prune for good air circulation, and apply fungicide during humid, wet-season periods where the disease has previously been a problem; growers should also avoid overhead irrigation late in the day, since leaves that stay wet overnight are more prone to infection.
